findings.text: The sentence says a codex stream "yields no tool-call timing at all", which the document's own table row at :118 contradicts (2.6% tool-call fallback) and the payload confirms as 4 of 155 runs (codex tool_call_timing is 151 no_timestamps and 0 no_calls), so four runs do carry timestamped tool calls and their shares come from the fallback the sentence says is unavailable.

The tests line records only the two ruff invocations, so the promotion gate receipt is built from a lint check and omits the --control-run command that is the done_when's quantitative measure, which survives only as a follow-up line in out/lint-and-rerun.log and in out/control.json.

tool_call_timing is set to "timestamped" whenever calls is non-empty, but _bash_calls_with_timing appends every call in `order` including one whose seconds is None (start or end absent at :208), so a stream that carries calls with no timestamps, or a call whose result never arrived, is labelled as timed when nothing in it can be charged; the label exists to separate absent timing from absent calls and it mislabels exactly that case.
